Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 2-day history of midline lower abdominal pain, mild urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; clinician suspected urinary tract infection and prescribed a 3-day antibiotic course.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain for 2 days; feels hot/sweaty.
- Associated symptoms: Mild nausea (no vomiting); increased thirst; mild increase in urinary frequency; pink-tinged urine. No dysuria, no back pain, no abnormal vaginal discharge, no upper abdominal pain or reflux.
- Bowel: Constipated last week; now normal. Last bowel movement 2 hours prior, normal. No blood in stool.
- Fever: Patient-measured temperature ~37°C one hour prior; no documented fevers.
- Gynecologic: Regular periods; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding. Prior internal contraceptive implant, now discontinued.
- Past medical history: No significant medical problems reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Medications: No regular or OTC medications.
- Family history: Mother with breast cancer (treated early).
- Social history: Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Alcohol: ~1 beer per occasion, ~4 times/week. No recent travel.

Examination:
- Vitals: Patient-reported temperature 37°C about one hour prior.
- Examination findings: Not performed (teleconsult).

Impression:
- Suspected urinary tract infection (UTI) presenting with lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, and hematuria; afebrile and no back pain reported.

Plan:
- Antibiotic therapy: 3-day course, twice daily; medication name and dose/route not documented. Prescription sent to patient’s allocated pharmacy.
- Start antibiotics as soon as available.
- Safety net: Seek care if pain worsens, fever develops, back pain occurs, new symptoms arise, symptoms do not improve, or if symptoms recur; may require face-to-face examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Pregnancy status/LMP, sexual history, objective vitals, abdominal and pelvic exam, urinalysis/urine culture, specific antibiotic name and dose/route, pain severity scale, hydration and analgesia advice.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some unclear audio and brief interruptions; overall key clinical details captured.
